transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get started. We need to finalize and record the revised retirement plan for the legacy webhook API before this meeting ends — this is a decision-bearing review, so we're not deferring approval. We all know the legacy API is scheduled for retirement next Friday, July 8, and the replacement API has hit 98 percent of observed traffic, which clears our normal migration-readiness threshold. The draft plan currently gives customers 7 days of notice and keeps the legacy endpoint available for 7 days after the announcement. Before I can approve this, I need to complete our standard deprecation review — so I'd like to check in with the API engineer and customer success. Who's representing those roles today?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I'm here as the API engineer, Maya. I actually need to flag something important before we approve this plan. I was investigating an unrelated latency spike and found telemetry showing three active integrators still sending legacy-webhook traffic. The largest one needs a 14-day parallel validation period plus hands-on migration support. I only confirmed the traffic identities minutes ago, so I haven't updated the deprecation ticket yet, but this directly affects the retirement timeline we're about to approve.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical on the customer success side. I confirmed with the account team this morning that the Northstar contract requires exactly 90 calendar days of notice, continued legacy-webhook availability through September 30, a sunset date of October 1, and exactly 30 days of legacy-endpoint overlap after the notice period expires. The customer record hasn't been updated yet because this confirmation came from a contract attachment I was reviewing for another renewal. This directly conflicts with the 7-day notice and 7-day overlap in the current draft plan.
transcript.speaker: A3
